title: Atlanta Braves Lose Reynaldo López and Face Pitching Crisis
seoTitle: Braves Lose Reynaldo López Amid Pitching Crisis
subtitle: With only 11 games remaining, the team tries to maintain its lead in the National League East.
excerpt: Reynaldo López's injury worsens the Atlanta Braves' pitching situation in the direct race for the National League East title.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Atlanta Braves face a moment of intense pressure in the final stretch of the Major League Baseball season, raising alarms about the team's standing in the leaderboard. The recent injury of pitcher Reynaldo López, placed on the 15-day injured list with right shoulder discomfort, has worsened the crisis of absences in the starting rotation. With only 11 games remaining in the regular season, the franchise is trying to protect its four-and-a-half-game lead in the National League East.

Reynaldo López's injury worsens pitching crisis

Reynaldo López was pulled in the third inning of the 7-3 loss to the Chicago Cubs. After the game, manager Walt Weiss revealed that the athlete will be rested due to right shoulder soreness. López had already missed the month of August due to a left knee issue and, this season, posts a 4.54 earned run average in 79 and a third innings. The previous year, he made only one appearance before undergoing season-ending shoulder surgery.

The direct race in the National League standings

Currently, the Atlanta Braves lead the East Division with a 4.5-game advantage over the Phillies. However, the team is 3.5 games behind the Dodgers in the race for the second direct postseason spot. With this scenario, it is likely the team will finish in third place and will need to play the Wild Card series at home, scheduled to begin on September 29, against the final National League qualifier.

Options to fill the vacancy in the starting rotation

To fill the vacancy left by López, right-handed pitcher JR Ritchie was called up from affiliate Gwinnett. Another internal option is AJ Smith-Shawver, who allowed just two runs over the last five innings of Monday's game. Currently, the only starting pitchers guaranteed in the postseason plans are Chris Sale, Tyler Mahle, Grant Holmes, and Martín Pérez, forcing the coaching staff to find quick solutions for the remaining games.

Challenges in the bullpen

The bullpen also shows instability in this final stretch. Robert Suarez has not pitched since late June, though he is already holding workout sessions, and Dylan Lee has not performed well for nearly two months. Young 21-year-old rookie Didier Fuentes emerges as an alternative to bridge games. Additionally, reliever Joe Jiménez was sent to begin his rehab assignment in Gwinnett, in his first official activity since the previous postseason.

With information from MLB.com, MLB Trade Rumors.
